fullName: PtychoProbe ptychography and X-ray fluorescence nanoprobe beamline at 33-ID-C

status2026.detail: PtychoProbe was the last APS-U feature beamline to be installed. First light was projected for October 2025. That month, the APS announced that commissioning had begun. In November 2025, the endstation instrument was still being installed. The APS Beamline Commissioning Progress chart lists '33-ID-C: PTYCHO' at stage 3, 'Ops Commissioning', on 26 Jan 2026. The chart does not define this label further. In the APS-U commissioning sequence, it covers shielding verification and first light. The station reached stage 4, technical commissioning, on 5 Oct 2026. It had not reached stage 5 for scientific commissioning and early experiments, or stage 6 for general users. The Beamline Directory lists 'Commissioning'. A 2026 APS March Meeting abstract described a 5 to 30 keV beam focused below 10 nm and anticipated user availability in mid-2026. That abstract was read only through a search-engine summary. The Aug 2025 schedule also projected general users in mid-2026, a few months before the current status. 33-ID-C appears in the General User proposal beamline list dated 7 Oct 2026. The late-January 2026 update described APS-U work as essentially completed, with all scope delivered and final DOE review pending. DOE announced formal project completion on 5 Feb 2026 after the CD-4 review in late Sept 2025. All feature beamlines met their Key Performance Parameters for source brightness at a defined energy and usable energy range. The 2026 Directory lists a 0.02 × 0.02 µm focus, equivalent to 20 nm. The 5 nm design goal is not yet claimed as delivered.

tagline: X-ray imaging of structure and elemental composition in chips, batteries and cells, with a 5 nm focus design goal.
summary: PtychoProbe is an X-ray microscope at the end of a 78-metre beamline in Sector 33 of Argonne's Advanced Photon Source, or APS. Hard X-rays from 5 to 30 keV are focused onto a sample and scanned across it. The design goal is a 5 nm spot, about the width of two DNA strands. Atoms emit X-rays at energies characteristic of their element, a process called fluorescence. These emissions are measured to map elemental composition, with a design sensitivity of a few atoms. Diffraction patterns are recorded at overlapping beam positions. From those patterns, a computer reconstructs an image by a method called ptychography. The resolution goal is toward 1 nm on samples that tolerate the radiation dose. X-ray penetration permits imaging of intact chips, batteries, catalysts and cement, including in 3D. In October 2026, the beamline is in technical commissioning, with a 20 nm focus listed so far.

whatAPSUEnables.text: X-rays are focused as they pass through a lens. The smallest focal spot depends on coherence, a stable phase relationship across the lens. With lower coherence, the focus is limited by the demagnified source image. Before the upgrade, coherent illumination required narrow slits. In high-resolution work at 2-ID-D, about 90% of the flux was blocked. The new horizontal electron beam is about 19 times narrower. Its nominal flat-beam root-mean-square width is 14.5 µm, compared with 275 µm before the upgrade. At 8 keV, the coherent fraction rises from about 0.08% to about 12%, and coherent flux increases by more than 100 times. Coherent illumination across 5 nm-class zone plates and multilayer Laue lenses is therefore possible, with more photons available for ptychography. The design projects about 1,000 times more photons per square nanometre in the focus, and scans up to 1,000 times faster. These projections assumed two undulators. Only one is installed, and the focus listed in 2026 is 20 nm.
quantitative: Horizontal electron source size decreases from σx ≈275 µm before the upgrade to 14.5 µm in the APS-U flat-beam model at 10% coupling, about 19× narrower. Nominal source parameters are σx = 14.5 µm, σx' = 2.75 µrad, σy = 3.1 µm, σy' = 1.29 µrad and εx = 39.7 pm·rad.
At 8 keV for a 4.8 m undulator, calculated coherent fraction increases from ~0.08% with the old lattice to ~11.6% with the MBA lattice.
More than two orders of magnitude increase in coherent flux relative to the pre-upgrade APS.
Projected focused flux density increases from ~10⁵ to 10⁶ ph/s/0.01%BW/nm² in a 50 nm pre-upgrade spot to ~10⁸ to 10⁹ ph/s/0.01%BW/nm² in a 5 nm spot.
Pre-upgrade 2-ID-D high-resolution operation used ~80 µm horizontal slits, blocking ~90% of the flux.
FDR predictions at SSA1 with coherence-length slit openings are 5.1 × 10¹² coherent ph/s with Si(111) at 10 keV, 7.5 × 10¹¹ ph/s with Si(311) at 10 keV and 2.5 × 10¹¹ ph/s with Si(111) at 25 keV.
FDR focused-flux predictions at 10 keV are 3.1 × 10¹⁰ ph/s in a 4 × 4 nm² FWHM spot with a 4 nm-zone ZP and Si(311), and 1.8 × 10¹¹ ph/s in a 10 × 10 nm² spot with a 16 nm ZP and Si(111).
Projected sample scan rates are up to 1,000× faster than at pre-upgrade APS beamlines.

Projected annual data volume is ~48.8 PB raw and 4.8 PB compressed, compared with ~0.73 PB/year across 2-ID-D ptychography, 2-ID-E and BNP XRF in the source document. It describes the increase as ~100×. Direct division gives ~67×.

techniques.name: Scanning X-ray fluorescence nanoprobe microscopy
techniques.text: Incident X-rays remove inner-shell electrons from atoms. When other electrons fill those vacancies, X-rays are emitted at energies characteristic of the element. This process is X-ray fluorescence, or XRF. The energies are measured with a silicon drift detector beside the sample at each scan position. Element maps are calculated from these spectra. With a 5 nm probe, the projected sensitivity is a few zinc atoms in a sample a few micrometres thick. The detector is placed close to the sample at 90° to the beam. Scattered background is weakest at 90° within the plane of horizontal polarization. Excitation up to 30 keV includes the K edges of elements through tin and the L or M lines of heavier elements. At 10 keV, the depth of focus for a 5 nm spot is only ±0.3 µm. Maps of thicker samples are projections. Fluorescence tomography is needed to recover the 3D distribution.

techniques.name: Ptychography with scanning coherent diffraction imaging
techniques.text: In ptychography, a coherent beam is scanned across a sample with successive positions typically overlapping by 60 to 70%. A far-field diffraction pattern is recorded at each position. Algorithms recover sample transmission in amplitude and phase, along with the beam profile, from all the patterns together. Resolution depends on the widest scattering angles at which enough photons are recorded. Intensity falls roughly as the inverse fourth power of scattering angle. A tenfold improvement in resolution therefore requires about 10,000 times more dose. Radiation tolerance limits the achievable resolution. Continuous scanning, called fly scanning, reduces time spent stopping and restarting. With this method, the APS Velociprobe prototype reached 8.8 nm resolution on a gold test pattern.

techniques.name: Ptychographic and fluorescence tomography in 3D
techniques.text: Scans repeated at hundreds of sample angles provide data for reconstruction of a 3D volume. Ptychographic and fluorescence data can both be used for tomography. The sample diameter limit is 3 mm. For 5 nm tomography, rotation must be known to about 40 µrad, equivalent to 0.0023°. Sample position during rotation must also be tracked to about a nanometre. The design includes anti-rotation references, tracking interferometers or rotating references measured by capacitive sensors. As a benchmark, ptychographic X-ray tomography of a 7 nm-node chip at the Paul Scherrer Institute, or PSI, reached 4 nm in 2024.

techniques.name: Spectro-microscopy / chemical-state mapping
techniques.text: Chemical states such as metallic and oxidized iron differ in their absorption spectra. To map these states, scans are repeated at energies across an absorption edge, where absorption increases sharply. The silicon monochromator bandwidth is about one part in 7,000. Zone-plate focal length is proportional to X-ray energy, so the optic position must change to maintain focus during an energy scan. Superconducting emission spectrometers with about 1 eV resolution are proposed for chemical-state measurements in a single scan. The required detectors are still in development.

techniques.name: Simultaneous multimodal XRF + ptychography
techniques.text: Fluorescence and diffraction are recorded during the same scan. The ptychographic image contains structural and density information. The fluorescence map contains elemental composition at the same positions. The reconstructed beam profile can be used to improve fluorescence resolution beyond the probe size. Mass and density from the phase image support quantitative fluorescence analysis. Fast scanning permits coarse surveys of large areas followed by finer scans of selected regions. The Beamline Directory lists simultaneous XRF and ptychography as a special capability.

scienceCases.title: Structure and chemistry inside computer chips
scienceCases.text: Chip features are only a few nanometres across. PtychoProbe is designed for imaging 3D wiring and mapping dopants, impurities and chemical states inside intact devices. Targets include contact interfaces, hafnium-oxide gate-insulator thickness, diffusion barriers and electromigration, the movement of metal atoms under electrical current. Benchmarks elsewhere include 4 nm ptychographic tomography of a 7 nm-node chip at the Paul Scherrer Institute in 2024. At the APS Hard X-ray Nanoprobe, streamed data were reconstructed by artificial intelligence at up to 2 kHz on a test pattern. Dedicated 3D chip imaging toward and below the 5 nm node is also planned for LYNX at 31-ID-E, complementing PtychoProbe.

scienceCases.title: Interfaces in batteries, fuel cells and electrolyzers
scienceCases.text: Performance and failure in batteries, fuel cells and electrolyzers depend on interfaces a few nanometres thick. Proposed PtychoProbe measurements include ion distributions, such as calcium, and metal chemical states in integrated devices, thin interfacial films and nanostructured electrodes. Conversion-type electrodes are among the targets. The 2023 first-experiments workshop included functional phases in fuel cells and water electrolyzers, electrode–electrolyte interfaces and metal films in electrochemical cells. Some proposals concerned other instruments. A 5 nm zone plate is only a few millimetres from the sample, restricting space for operating cells. At the In Situ Nanoprobe, or ISN, at 19-ID, the mirrors are 61 mm from the focus, providing more clearance for such experiments.

scienceCases.title: Individual catalyst particles in 3D
scienceCases.text: About 90% of chemical products are made with catalysts. Images of individual catalyst nanoparticles inside millimetre-sized pellets would give particle size, shape and chemistry, including contact with the supporting material. These measurements inform catalyst design. Hard X-rays are required to reach the absorption edges of noble metals such as ruthenium, rhodium, palladium, silver, platinum and gold. The PtychoProbe goals are 3D chemical imaging down to 5 nm with fluorescence and finer structural imaging with ptychography.

scienceCases.title: Cement hydration and crack formation
scienceCases.text: Concrete failure involves defects that grow into cracks. Portland cement production emits about 5% of global CO₂. Imaging cement-grain reactions, hardening and deterioration at 5 nm could inform more durable, lower-carbon materials. Earlier APS work combined nano-tomography and nano-fluorescence to measure the 3D structure, chemistry and density of hydrating tricalcium silicate grains, a main cement ingredient. Those measurements covered the induction period early in hydration.

scienceCases.title: Brain tissue and cellular chemistry
scienceCases.text: X-ray penetration through blocks of brain tissue could permit 3D tracing of neurons without sectioning. The goal is resolution below 10 nm over volumes of 100 µm³ and more. A cubic millimetre at 10 nm voxels would contain about a petabyte of data. Radiation damage limits frozen, hydrated biological samples to about 10 nm resolution. PtychoProbe's finer-resolution goals therefore concern more radiation-tolerant samples. Earlier work at the APS Bionanoprobe combined 3D fluorescence and ptychographic tomography of whole frozen Chlamydomonas cells to map metals in this green alga.

scienceCases.title: Micrometeorites and environmental particles
scienceCases.text: Nanoscale grains in micrometeorites and comet dust contain evidence of early Solar System conditions. Nanoparticles in soils and ashes contain toxic or valuable metals. Proposed measurements at PtychoProbe include elemental composition and chemical states in micrometeorites about 10 µm across, microbial and mineral effects on contaminant chemistry, and metals in phytoplankton. Workshop proposals also included resource potential and risks of coal-ash waste, and thin-film solar cells such as perovskites.

keyParameters.label: Techniques
keyParameters.value: Ptychography, X-ray fluorescence microscopy, tomography; simultaneous ptychography + XRF; 3D nano-imaging

keyParameters.label: Installed source
keyParameters.value: One planar HPM revolver APS21R25#3 in the downstream DS position; upstream position empty. APS21#8 has 2.1 cm period, E1 8.34 keV and K 1.38. APS25#6 has 2.5 cm period, E1 4.59 keV and K 1.99. These values are at the 8.5 mm device minimum gap; length is ~2.35 m.
keyParameters.note: In the ID table 'DS-1'/'DS-2' are the two magnet structures of the one downstream device, not two positions. Current user minimum gap 8.9 mm. FDR baseline: two in-line revolvers, 4.6 m total.

keyParameters.label: Front end
keyParameters.value: Windowless HHL front end with differential pumping. Exit mask opening 2 × 2 mm horizontally × vertically at 25.4 m. Tungsten exit collimator opening 5 × 5 mm at 26.1 m.
keyParameters.note: HHLFE limits 21 kW, 590 kW/mrad².

keyParameters.label: Monochromator
keyParameters.value: Horizontally deflecting LN₂-cooled double-crystal Si(111), ΔE/E ≈ 1.4 × 10⁻⁴, fixed exit, 1 mm offset
keyParameters.note: Offset and cooling are from the FDR. Its optics text specifies a standard Si(111) HDCM. Si(311) appears only in flux, coherence and heat-load calculations in Tables 4.41 to 4.42 and Figs. 4.33, 4.36. Its ΔE/E is ~3 × 10⁻⁵, often rounded to 10⁻⁵ in the PDR. The FDR component table also includes a Mo/B₄C double-multilayer monochromator at 31.9 m. Neither Si(311) nor the DMM is listed in 2026, and installation is unconfirmed. The Directory also gives 1.4 × 10⁻⁴ for the Si(111) HDCM at 2-ID-D.

keyParameters.label: Secondary sources
keyParameters.value: SSA/BDA1 at 47.9 m in 33-ID-B for best focus; SSA/BDA2 at 57.8 m in 33-ID-C for the flux/resolution trade-off.
keyParameters.note: Water-cooled apertures with ±50 µm range, 100 nm resolution and repeatability. The 2017 PDR positions were 40 m and 60 m.

keyParameters.label: Transverse coherence length at SSA1

keyParameters.note: SRW wave-optics, 2018 source parameters, 4.6 m source.

keyParameters.label: Nanofocusing optics
keyParameters.value: Four-zone-plate carrier covering 5 to 8, 8 to 12, 12 to 18 and 18 to 30 keV. Multilayer Laue lenses have a separate carrier. Zone plates are preferred at lower energy and MLLs above 13 keV.
keyParameters.note: The Directory lists Fresnel zone plates and multilayer Laue lenses as focusing options.

keyParameters.value: Δr_N 4 nm, D 180 µm, f 5.8 mm, 1900 nm thick, 33% efficiency, 11,250 zones
keyParameters.note: At 25 keV: D 72 µm, f 5.81 mm, 4400 nm, 4500 zones.

keyParameters.label: Flux

insertionDevices.name: APS21R25#3 revolver, 2.1 cm structure APS21#8, table row 'DS-1'
insertionDevices.type: planar hybrid permanent-magnet revolver undulator with two selectable structures on one rotating support
insertionDevices.notes: In the Sector 33 straight, the downstream DS position is occupied and upstream US position empty in Sep 2026. Table rows DS-1 and DS-2 refer to APS21#8 and APS25#6 within this one device. Design minimum gap is 8.5 mm in table note 7. Current administrative and user minimum gap is 8.9 mm, though the row is partly garbled. At 8.5 mm, K_eff = 1.38, E1 = 8.34 keV, power density is 216 kW/mrad² and total power 5.4 kW at 200 mA. The S33 period count is garbled. Identical devices at S08/S09 have 112 periods, from which ~2.35 m length is inferred. FDR Table 4.47 uses K = 1.305 and E1 = 8.8 keV for U21.

insertionDevices.name: APS21R25#3 revolver, 2.5 cm structure APS25#6, table row 'DS-2'
insertionDevices.type: second planar hybrid permanent-magnet structure, selected by 90° support rotation
insertionDevices.notes: At 8.5 mm gap, K_eff = 1.99, E1 = 4.59 keV, power density is 225 kW/mrad² and total power 8.0 kW. The inferred period count is 94, based on S08/S09 devices. First-harmonic operation covers the 5 keV low-energy end. The FDR maximum power through the 2 × 2 mm mask is 2.28 kW for the 4.6 m baseline at Ky = 1.939. About half that power is estimated for the single installed device.

insertionDevices.name: FDR baseline of two in-line Rev 2.5/2.1 revolvers and phase shifter, 4.6 m total; installation differs
insertionDevices.type: planar HPM revolver undulators, dual in-line
insertionDevices.notes: FDR Ch. 3 Table 3.13 lists two in-line Rev 2.5/2.1 devices with phase shifter/corrector. Ch. 4 Table 4.38 specifies 4.6 m total, 21/25 mm periods and a source at the straight centre. The 2017 PDR instead proposed a 29 mm HGVPU with horizontal gap and vertical polarization for σ-geometry operation of the horizontal monochromator.

source.canting: No canting magnets are used. The beam path follows the straight-section axis. Two in-line revolvers and a phase shifter were planned in the FDR. Only the downstream position is filled as of Sep 2026.
source.frontEnd: The windowless APS-U High-Heat-Load Front End, or HHLFE, includes differential pumping. Design limits for two in-line undulators are 21 kW total and 590 kW/mrad² peak. The sequence in FDR Fig. 3.2 is LPPS lead-lined photon shutter, storage-ring valve, BTFM1 burn-through mask, fixed masks FM2/FM3, collimator, GRID-XBPM1, photon shutter PS2 with intensity monitor IM1, safety shutters SS1&SS2, ratchet-wall collimator, front-end valve, exit mask with XBPM2, tungsten exit collimator and beamline isolation valve. Exit-mask opening is 2 × 2 mm at 25.4 m. The exit-collimator opening is 5 × 5 mm at 26.1 m, narrowed to limit bremsstrahlung with small-offset monochromators. The exit table is inside 33-ID-A. A residual gas analyser is required in the first optics enclosure for windowless operation.
source.sourceSizeAndDivergence: Nominal electron parameters at an ID straight in Aug 2024 are as follows. Flat-beam mode at κ = 0.1 has σx = 14.5 µm, σx' = 2.75 µrad, σy = 3.08 µm and σy' = 1.29 µrad, with εx = 39.7 pm·rad and εy = 4.0 pm·rad. Round-beam mode at κ = 1 has σx = 12.3 µm, σx' = 2.34 µrad, σy = 8.26 µm and σy' = 3.47 µrad, with 28.7 pm·rad emittance in each plane. Natural emittance is 41.5 pm·rad. For L ≈2.35 m at 10 keV, the calculated single-electron photon terms are σr = √(2λL)/4π ≈1.9 µm and σr' = √(λ/2L) ≈5.1 µrad. Combined flat-beam photon source estimates are 14.6 × 3.6 µm and 5.8 × 5.3 µrad. The horizontal source is ~4.7× wider than the vertical, reducing relative sensitivity to horizontal angular errors. FDR calculations used Borland's Oct 2018 CD-2 parameters. For a flat beam over 5 to 25 keV, calculated single-2.35 m to design-4.6 m scale factors are ~0.5 for central-cone flux and ~0.34 for brightness/coherent flux. The shorter device has greater photon divergence and less favorable beta matching.

branches.name: Single in-line 33-ID PtychoProbe beamline
branches.description: The beam path runs from the HHL front end through 33-ID-A, with slits, M1, DCM, optional design DMM, M2 and masks. Shielded transport leads to SSA/BDA1 and pink/mono shutters in 33-ID-B, then through mini-hutches to 33-ID-C. That station contains SSA/BDA2, the vacuum instrument, the 5.6 m detector mover and beam stop. Mirror curvature selects either the best-focus source image at SSA1, 47.9 m from the source and ~22 m from the lens, or the flux/resolution position at SSA2, 57.8 m from the source and ~12 m from the lens. Pink-beam-rated masks, shutters and beam stop permit mirror-only or multilayer operation in the FDR design.

components.name: Revolver undulator APS21R25#3, 2.1 cm / 2.5 cm periods
components.distanceNote: Approximate. The device occupies the downstream half of the straight. The ID vacuum chamber is 5.363 m flange to flange, with nominally 4.8 m undulator space in FDR Fig. 3.10 and Sec. 3-3.2. Placement is from the APS ID table. Its centre is estimated at +1.3 m from the straight-section centre used for FDR distances. The 4.6 m FDR baseline was centred on the straight.
components.text: In the alternating magnetic field of this 2.35-metre device, 6 GeV electrons follow an oscillating path and emit a narrow X-ray beam. The device is a revolver undulator. Magnet arrays with 2.1 and 2.5 cm periods share a rotating support. To change arrays, the gap is opened and the support rotated. The 2.5 cm array's first-harmonic energy is 4.6 keV at the minimum gap. Together with higher harmonics, the two arrays cover 5 to 30 keV. Only one device is installed in the downstream half of the straight section. The design assumed two in line, totaling 4.6 m.

components.name: Front-end GRID beam position monitor XBPM1
components.distanceNote: Approximate and generic: the high-heat-load front-end component order follows FDR Fig. 3.2. No 33-ID-specific position is published; the value is a placeholder for the model.
components.text: Beam position is measured in the front end for accelerator feedback, with stability of a few micrometres. This grazing-incidence GRID monitor is used with two others downstream. Its position here is a generic placeholder.

components.name: Front-end photon shutter PS2 and safety shutters SS1/SS2
components.distanceNote: Approximate and generic: order from FDR Fig. 3.2, just upstream of the ratchet wall. No 33-ID-specific value is published.
components.text: Beam heat is absorbed in a water-cooled photon shutter. High-energy radiation is blocked by two independent tungsten safety shutters behind it, permitting entry to the hutches. All three are interlocked with the personnel safety system.

components.name: Storage-ring ratchet wall and collimator
components.distanceNote: Approximate. The FOE upstream wall is ~23.6 m in FDR Fig. 4.31. Wall thickness is assumed ~1.5 m, similar to other sectors.
components.text: A thick concrete shield wall separates the accelerator tunnel from the experiment hall. The beam passes through a small opening lined with a metal collimator. Radiation outside that opening is blocked. Wall position and thickness here are estimates.

components.name: Front-end exit mask and XBPM2, 2 × 2 mm
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.39.
components.text: The central beam passes through a 2 × 2 mm opening in a water-cooled metal block. Radiation outside the opening is absorbed as heat. Beam pointing is measured by a built-in position monitor. Differential pumping separates beamline and ring vacuum without a beryllium window.

components.name: Front-end tungsten exit collimator, 5 × 5 mm
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.39.
components.text: Radiation outside a 5 × 5 mm opening is absorbed in thick tungsten. This includes bremsstrahlung, high-energy radiation produced when electrons interact with residual gas in the ring. The narrowed aperture limits this radiation in beamlines with small monochromator offsets.

components.name: HHL white-beam slits 33ID-SL-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.39.
components.text: The beam is restricted by adjustable tungsten-edged jaws before the first mirror. This reduces heat load on the mirror. Design studies used openings of 2 × 2 mm and 0.5 × 0.5 mm.

components.name: M1 high-heat-load horizontal focusing mirror
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.39; the 2024 elevation drawing labels M1 at ~28.2 m.
components.text: X-rays meet the silicon surface at a grazing angle of 2.5 mrad, about one seventh of a degree. Reflection changes beam direction horizontally. About 330 to 450 W is absorbed as heat. Curvature is adjusted to focus the beam horizontally onto a micrometre-sized aperture 20 to 30 m downstream. Bending also corrects thermal deformation of the surface. Slope errors, small surface-angle deviations, are kept below 0.1 µrad. Silicon, rhodium and platinum stripes are selected to reject higher harmonics at multiples of the chosen energy.

components.name: Lead secondary scattering collimator 33ID-SC-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.39.
components.text: X-rays scattered from the first mirror are absorbed in lead shielding. This is secondary-radiation shielding, separate from the direct beam path.

components.name: Pink-beam mis-steering mask 33ID-PM-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.39.
components.text: The mirror-reflected pink beam is blocked here if it is mis-steered. The mask is immediately downstream of the first mirror.

components.name: Beam position monitor and fluorescent flag 33ID-BD-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.39.
components.text: Beam position and alignment are checked using a retractable fluorescent screen and position monitor between the first mirror and monochromator.

components.name: Horizontal double-crystal monochromator 33ID-MN-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.39; the 2024 drawing shows the 'DCM' at ~30.5 m.
components.text: A narrow X-ray energy band, about one part in 7,000, is selected by two silicon crystals. Diffraction is horizontal. Floor vibrations are smaller horizontally, and the source is wider in this plane, reducing sensitivity to angular motion. The incident X-rays are horizontally polarized. Horizontal diffraction occurs in π geometry, with about 70% of vertical-reflection throughput at 6 keV and over 90% above 10 keV. Liquid nitrogen is used for crystal cooling. Installation of a narrower-band Si(311) pair is unconfirmed.

specs.crystals: Si(111) in FDR specification; Si(311) only in calculations, installation unconfirmed
specs.Throughput in π geometry: ≈70% of σ at 6 keV; >90% above 10 keV for Si(111)

components.name: Nanofocusing zone plates and multilayer Laue lenses

components.text: Nanometre focusing occurs by diffraction through zone plates or multilayer Laue lenses. A Fresnel zone plate has thousands of concentric metal rings, typically gold. A multilayer Laue lens is a thin section of stacked nanometre layers, with focusing in one direction. Outermost zone width sets zone-plate resolution. The ideal 5 nm design at 10 keV has 4 nm outer zones, 11,250 zones, a 180 µm diameter and a 5.8 mm focal length. Focal position changes with energy, so the optics are mounted on a movable gantry. Four zone plates cover 5 to 30 keV. Multilayer Laue lenses are preferred above 13 keV. The optic is under 0.2 mm across and is enlarged in the drawing.

instruments.name: PtychoProbe scanning X-ray nanoprobe and ptychography endstation
instruments.text: Optics and sample stages are mounted on air-bearing granite blocks within a vacuum chamber. X-rays are focused by a zone plate or multilayer Laue lens. The sample is scanned through the beam at up to 7 mm/s. Relative optic and sample positions are measured to about 1 nm by interferometry. Fluorescence spectra and diffraction patterns are recorded during the scan. Sample rotation through ±180° permits 3D measurements. Real-time control applies feedback and feed-forward position corrections, triggers detectors and calculates preliminary low-resolution reconstructions. Cooling, a flow cell and electrical connections were planned. Their installation is unconfirmed.

Six interferometer axes were logged 25,000 times per second. Relative vibration of the optics gantry and sample stage was 0.75 to 1.4 nm root mean square over 5 to 100 Hz. Measured resolution was 8.8 nm on a gold test pattern and about 10 nm on a chip at 3,000 frames per second. A VelociProbe endstation is listed at 33-ID-C in the 2026 Directory. Relocation from 2-ID-D is otherwise undocumented.

geometryNotes:
PtychoProbe has a single beam path without canting. One revolver undulator occupies the downstream half of the Sector 33 straight. The high-heat-load front end is windowless. Its exit table is inside 33-ID-A.

The main optics occupy 33-ID-A from 23.6 to 36.0 m. At M1, 28.3 m from the source, horizontal deflection is 5 mrad, twice the 2.5 mrad incidence angle. The DCM and design DMM have about 1 mm horizontal offset. At M2, 33.1 m from the source, vertical deflection is 5 mrad. From these FDR distances, calculated axis displacement is about 34 mm horizontally and 10 mm vertically at the 35 m FOE exit, and 0.21 m horizontally and 0.18 m vertically at the 69.7 m sample. Deflection senses inboard or outboard and upward or downward are undocumented. The exhibit therefore uses a straight axis, as in the published drawings.

Downstream enclosures are in line. SSA1 is in 33-ID-B, spanning 41.2 to 52.1 m with width about 1.7 m. SSA2 is at the entrance to 33-ID-C, spanning 57.4 to 77.6 m with width about 4 m. About 12 m of transport precedes the instrument at 69.7 m. The 5.6 m detector tank extends to about 76.7 m, with the beam stop at the end wall. Shielded pipes connect the enclosures past mini-hutches A-MH-1, B-MH-1 and C-MH-1 in the 2024 drawing.

In the FDR plan, 33-BM-B/C lie inboard of the ID line. The 33-ID-C control room and vestibule are along its inboard wall. Neighbouring-sector hutches are angled on the outboard side.

Beam height at the ID straight is 1.400 m in FDR Fig. 3.10. Hall beam height at 33-ID is unpublished. M2's 5 mrad vertical deflection corresponds to a sample-height shift of about 0.18 m, with sign unknown.

FDR 2019 distances are measured from the straight-section centre. The 2024 elevation drawing predates instrument installation in Nov 2025 and is a late-design drawing. It agrees within about 0.5 m except for BDA2 at about 57.5 to 59 m and the detector mover at about 70.6 to 76.7 m. It is not an as-built record.

The exhibit's stepped and tapered 33-ID-A outline, chamfered 33-ID-C outline, control room starting near 54.4 m, mini-hutch heights, instrument stages and detector tank are scaled from FDR Figs. 4.31/4.37 and the 2024 elevation drawing, with uncertainty ±0.2 m. The zone plate, OSA and crystal offsets are enlarged for visibility.

interactiveIdeas.title: Secondary-source aperture and focal size
interactiveIdeas.concept: Adjust an aperture slider to compare the source image at SSA1, the resulting focal spot and transmitted flux. Focal size is calculated from the demagnified aperture and the lens Airy pattern. Switch between the old APS horizontal source width of 275 µm and the APS-U width of 14.5 µm. With the old source, narrow-aperture focusing has much lower transmission.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: How coherence, source brightness and slit opening determine focal size and transmitted flux.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Spot model from the PDR: s = √(s_demag² + s_diff²). Aperture image size is s_demag = Δ·(f/z), with z ≈21.8 m from SSA1 to lens or ~12 m from SSA2. For a 5 nm ZP at 10 keV, f = 5.8 mm and demagnification is ~3,800×. Diffraction resolution is ≈1.22·Δr_N by the Rayleigh criterion, or ~Δr_N FWHM. Coherent illumination across diameter D requires Δ ≲ λz/(πD) = 4.82 µm in the FDR. Calculated source-image magnifications at SSA1 are ≈0.69 horizontally and ≈0.45 vertically. The flat-beam 10 keV image is ~24 × ~4 µm FWHM, so aperture restriction mainly limits horizontal flux. Transmission follows the Gaussian integral across the opening. Coherent flux saturates above the 2.9 × 3.0 µm coherence lengths at 10 keV. The PDR estimates that aperture motion equal to 10% of opening changes focal position by 10% of spot size. Old horizontal parameters are σx = 275 µm and σx' = 11 µrad; APS-U σx = 14.5 µm.

interactiveIdeas.title: Zone-plate geometry and energy bandwidth
interactiveIdeas.concept: Change X-ray energy from 5 to 30 keV, outermost zone width from 4 to 60 nm and diameter from 50 to 250 µm. Inspect the ring count, focal length, spot size, depth of focus and required energy bandwidth. A zoomable sector displays the zone geometry. Switch between Si(111) and Si(311) bandwidths. Red indicates a bandwidth wider than the optic tolerates. Presets contain the FDR 5 nm and 20 nm designs.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: How zone width sets resolution and energy changes focal length. Why 5 nm focusing requires difficult fabrication and narrow bandwidth for many-zone optics.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Zone-plate equations: λ[nm] = 1.23984/E[keV]; f = D·Δr_N/λ; N = D/(4Δr_N); NA = λ/(2Δr_N); Rayleigh resolution ≈1.22·Δr_N; depth of focus ±2Δr_N²/λ. Chromatic requirement is λ/Δλ ≥ N. FDR Table 4.45 has a 4 nm-zone optic at 10 keV with D = 180 µm, f = 5.8 mm and N = 11,250; at 25 keV, D = 72 µm, f = 5.81 mm and N = 4,500. Si(111) bandwidth ΔE/E ≈1.4 × 10⁻⁴ allows N ≲7,000. Si(311) bandwidth is about 3 × 10⁻⁵. Mark the 5 nm preset as bandwidth-limited with Si(111) at 10 keV, but not at 25 keV. Ideal binary phase-zone-plate efficiency is ≤~40%. The FDR assumes 33% at thickness 1900 nm for 10 keV and 4400 nm for 25 keV. Aspect ratios of ~475 to 1100 motivate crossed 1D MLLs and conic/volume zone plates. Central stop and order-sorting aperture suppress unwanted orders. The 5 nm depth of focus at 10 keV is ±0.3 µm.

interactiveIdeas.title: Ptychographic reconstruction from overlapping patterns
interactiveIdeas.concept: Scan a model chip or cell with a displayed probe footprint. A diffraction pattern is calculated at each position. Adjust overlap and photon counts, then run in-browser ePIE to recover the image and probe. Below about 50% overlap or at low photon counts, reconstruction fails or resolution decreases.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: How diffraction data are reconstructed into an image, why overlap and coherence matter, and how photon counts and radiation tolerance limit resolution.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Far-field intensity is I(q) = |F{P(r − r_j)·O(r)}|². ePIE updates the object and probe alternately. Reconstruction pixel Δx = λz/(N·p); for 10 keV, 155 mm and 512 × 75 µm sampling, it is 0.5 nm. Overlap relaxes ptychographic oversampling requirements, but each pattern must still sample the probe speckle scale. Typical overlap is 60 to 70%, with step ≲0.3 to 0.4 of probe diameter. The FDR uses 66%. Resolution follows the highest q with adequate SNR. With Porod-like I ∝q⁻⁴, a 10× improvement requires ~10⁴× more photons. Include Poisson noise. Retain phase wrapping, overall phase and position ambiguities, partial-coherence mixed-state probes, interferometer-derived position errors and fly-scan blur.

interactiveIdeas.title: Fluorescence spectra and element maps
interactiveIdeas.concept: Scan a model circuit with copper and tungsten lines and arsenic-doped regions, based on PDR Fig. 6.61. Compare a 50 nm pre-upgrade nanoprobe beam and a 5 nm PtychoProbe design beam. Photon counts accumulate in an energy spectrum. Place windows around peaks to calculate element maps. Tune incident energy above or below the As K edge to compare arsenic excitation.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: How fluorescence energies identify elements, why excitation requires sufficient incident energy, and how beam size determines spatial averaging.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Line energies are Cu Kα 8.05 keV with K edge 8.98 keV, Zn Kα 8.64 keV, As Kα 10.54 keV with K edge 11.87 keV, W Lα 8.40 keV and Lβ 9.67 keV with L3 edge 10.21 keV, and Fe Kα 6.40 keV. Excitation must exceed the relevant edge. Include overlapping W Lα and Cu/Zn peaks, and As Kα with Pb Lα at 10.55 keV. Counts are Poisson-distributed. Detection limit is ~3σ above background. Signal is proportional to flux × dwell × concentration × cross-section × solid angle. Horizontal 90° geometry minimizes elastic background for horizontal polarization. At 10 keV, 5 nm optics have ±0.3 µm depth of focus. Thick samples produce projection maps. The sensitivity projection is a few Zn atoms in samples a few micrometres thick.

interactiveIdeas.title: Vibration and thermal position error
interactiveIdeas.concept: Compare a 5 nm beam and a 5 nm feature. Add floor vibration, air flow from a hutch door or a 0.1 °C temperature change, and inspect focal-position error and image blur. Apply modeled granite stages, air-bearing venting, interferometer feedback and temperature control to compare their contributions to the error budget.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: How position stability limits nanoscale imaging and why material choice, vacuum, reflection geometry and laser metrology matter.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Thermal expansion is ΔL = α·L·ΔT. The PDR gives ~230 nm expansion for 10 cm aluminium and ~60 nm for granite after a 0.1 °C change. Hutch stability target is 0.1 °C/24 h and floor background <20 nm rms over 2 to 100 Hz. Velociprobe relative vibration was 1.4 nm rms in X and 0.75 nm rms in Y over 5 to 100 Hz. PtychoProbe fly-scan precision is <2.5 nm and metrology accuracy 1 nm. Source horizontal-to-vertical size ratios are ~4.7× in flat-beam and ~1.5× in round-beam modes. Larger source width reduces relative sensitivity to angular errors, and floor vibration is smaller horizontally. At the SSA, upstream optic vibration mainly changes transmitted intensity, with less focal-position motion.

interactiveIdeas.title: Scan speed, frame rate and data volume
interactiveIdeas.concept: Set scan speed and detector frame rate for a 1 mm² chip region at 5 nm detail. Compare exposure blur, overlap and map time. A data-rate display accumulates storage volume during the scan.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: How continuous scanning, detector speed and computation determine map area, resolution and acquisition time.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Scan speed v = step × frame rate, with step = d_probe·(1 − overlap). A 20 nm probe, 66% overlap and 1 MHz frame rate give ~6.8 mm/s, consistent with the FDR 7 mm/s limit and Directory ≤7 mm/s listing. EIGER2 XE 1.5M frames are ~3 MB at 2 kHz, about 6 GB/s. A 200 × 200 fast detector at 30 kHz produces ≈2.4 GB/s. Annual raw volume is ≈48.8 PB. The Velociprobe benchmark is 3 kHz frames, 10 nm resolution and ~9 × 10⁴ resolution elements/s. PSI 2024 achieved 14,000 resolution elements/s at 4 nm. Mixed-state or multi-mode probe reconstruction represents exposure motion. Detector duty cycle matters; SELUN is >98.8%.

interactiveIdeas.title: Horizontal monochromator geometry
interactiveIdeas.concept: Compare vertical diffraction in σ geometry with horizontal diffraction in π geometry for horizontally polarized X-rays. Change photon energy to compare throughput. Add 0.1 µrad angular motion in each plane to inspect focal-position error.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: How polarization and source dimensions affect the balance between low-energy flux and position stability.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Bragg relation is λ = 2d·sinθ_B, with d(Si 111) = 3.1356 Å and d(Si 311) = 1.6375 Å. The dynamical π-polarization factor |cos 2θ_B| vanishes at θ_B = 45°, corresponding to 2.80 keV for Si(111) and 5.35 keV for Si(311). Two-crystal throughput relative to σ geometry is ≈0.70 at 6 keV and 0.91 at 10 keV for Si(111), and 0.66 at 10 keV for Si(311). This informed the PDR 2017 vertical-polarization proposal and is consistent with the installed Si(111)-only listing. Mirror angular error δ changes image position by 2δ·q. For a DCM, common rotation of both crystals preserves exit direction. Relative crystal angle δrel causes shift 2δrel·q. Relative sensitivity depends on source dimensions in that plane, with flat-beam σx ≈14.5 µm and σy ≈3.1 µm.

funFacts: The 5 nm zone-plate design at 10 keV has 11,250 rings within a 180 µm disc, about the width of two human hairs. These values are from FDR Table 4.45.

A 0.1 °C temperature increase expands a 10 cm aluminium part by 230 nm and granite by 60 nm. These shifts are 12 to 46 times the 5 nm focus goal. Granite construction and hutch temperature control reduce thermal-position error.
The detectors move on rails inside a 5.6-metre vacuum tank. The minimum fast-detector distance is 75 mm behind the sample. The large-detector maximum distance is 5 metres.
At 10 keV, the depth of focus for 5 nm resolution is about ±0.3 µm, about 1/100 of a human hair width. Most samples are thicker than this focused region.
The granite blocks move on air cushions during positioning. After venting, they rest in granite-to-granite contact. Vertical motion uses granite wedges with a 5.5° design angle.
At the pre-upgrade 2-ID-D microprobe in Sector 2, across the ring, high-resolution focusing required narrow slits that blocked about 90% of the X-rays.
Two arrays with 2.1 and 2.5 cm periods share the revolver undulator support. To change arrays, the gap is opened and the support rotated.

The projected annual raw data volume is 48.8 petabytes. The APS document describes this as roughly 100 times the ~0.73 PB/year of three earlier microscopy instruments. Direct division gives about 67 times.
Imaging one cubic millimetre of brain at 10 nm voxels would produce about a petabyte of data.
PtychoProbe was the last APS-U feature beamline installed. Endstation installation was still underway in November 2025.
The APS feature page gives size comparisons for the 5 nm resolution target. DNA thickness is about 2.5 nm and paper thickness about 100,000 nm. The ptychographic resolution goal is toward 1 nm.
Relative vibration of the Velociprobe granite optics and sample stages was 1.4 nm and 0.75 nm rms over 5 to 100 Hz. Measured resolution on a gold test pattern was 8.8 nm.

openQuestions: As of Sep 2026, only one APS21R25#3 revolver is installed, downstream in Sector 33. DS-1 and DS-2 are its two magnet structures. The FDR baseline was two in-line devices totaling 4.6 m. Plans for a second device are undocumented. The S33 period count is garbled; 112/94 periods are inferred from identical S08/S09/S19/S20 devices. A calculated Gaussian-beam estimate suggests that FDR central-cone flux is about 2× and brightness/coherent flux about 3× higher than for the installed source. The Directory's 10¹¹ ph/s at 10 keV is consistent with the single device.

The 2026 Directory lists a DCM with ΔE/E = 1.4 × 10⁻⁴ for Si(111). The FDR optics specification also names standard Si(111), while Si(311) appears only in calculations. The FDR component table includes a Mo/B₄C double-multilayer monochromator at 31.9 m. Only M1/DCM/M2 are labelled in the 2024 elevation. Installation of Si(311) crystals or the DMM is unconfirmed.

The PDR proposed vertical polarization for the horizontal DCM. The FDR switched to a standard horizontally polarized revolver. Si(311)-class bandwidth for 4 nm-zone optics over 5 to 8 keV is undocumented. In this range, π-geometry Si(311) reflectivity falls sharply.
FDR text locates PtychoProbe at 33-ID-D. Its figures and the 2026 Directory use 33-ID-C, which is used here.

The Directory lists VelociProbe at 33-ID-C with zone-plate focusing, 5 to 20 nm ptychography and air-bearing rotation below 50 nm runout. Papers place the Velociprobe at 2-ID-D, mostly for pre-upgrade data. The current 2-ID-D listing omits it. Relocation to 33-ID-C for commissioning or a second instrument is unconfirmed.

The Directory lists a 20 × 20 nm focus in 2026. Installation and commissioning of 5 nm-class zone plates or multilayer Laue lenses are unconfirmed. Use of conic zone plates from the APS Optics LDRD program is also unpublished.

As-built mirror cooling, radii and deflection senses are unpublished. PDR LN₂ cooling differs from FDR notched side-cooling. Inboard/outboard and up/down deflection directions are unknown. These details are schematic in the exhibit.

The 2024 XRF plan names Vortex ME7. The Directory lists only an Energy Dispersive Detector. No installation status is available for the FDR/PDR backscatter detector, capillary-collimated detector or superconducting emission spectrometer.

The FDR lists possible cooling, flow-cell and electrical-feedthrough environments, and vacuum/He/N₂/Ar/air atmospheres. Cryogenic sample operation is unconfirmed for PtychoProbe in 2026. It is offered at the 2-ID-D Bionanoprobe.

The 2019 FDR and 2024 drawing differ in BDA2 position, 57.8 m versus ~57.5 to 59 m, and detector-mover span, 70.0 to 76.5 m versus ~70.6 to 76.7 m. Unidentified 2024 items include a red-outlined box at ~60 to 61.3 m and two stands 1000 mm apart at ~67 to 68 m in 33-ID-C. Functions of the three mini-hutches are undocumented.
33-ID-specific positions for XBPM1, front-end shutters and ratchet wall are unpublished. Component-list positions are generic placeholders.

The APS March Meeting 2026 abstract and Aug 2025 update projected users in mid-2026. The abstract was read only via a search summary. The 5 Oct 2026 chart still lists stage 4 technical commissioning. The date of first early-science experiments is unknown.
Measured focus size, coherent flux and ptychographic resolution at 33-ID remain unpublished as of Oct 2026.

DECTRIS specifies the SELUN Si sensor for 8 to 30 keV, with thresholds from 4.6 keV. Ptychography over 5 to 8 keV is undocumented. Possible EIGER2 XE use or SELUN operation below its nominal range is unconfirmed.

The Directory describes VelociProbe at 33-ID-C with the phrase 'Fresnel zone plate focusing for micron-size beams'. This may refer to a defocused or large-beam ptychography-poly mode. The meaning is unexplained.
